Venezuelan Oil & Gas Sector Sees Fresh Investment as PetroAndina Launches Expansion

Caracas—Venezuela’s oil and gas sector is set for renewed growth as PetroAndina, a leading national energy producer, announced on Thursday a $450 million investment to expand crude output in the prolific Orinoco Belt. The move is being seen as a sign of market confidence in the country’s hydrocarbons industry, following a steady uptick in production figures over the past year.

According to PetroAndina’s chief executive, Mariela Contreras, the new capital will be deployed over the next 24 months to upgrade extraction infrastructure, develop enhanced oil recovery techniques, and modernize key transport pipelines in the Ayacucho and Junín fields. “This expansion marks a significant step in our long-term commitment to Venezuela’s oil and gas future,” Contreras said at a press briefing in Caracas. “We are focused on efficiency and sustainability, ensuring higher yields while maintaining our environmental standards.”

Industry analysts suggest that PetroAndina’s expansion could add as much as 45,000 barrels per day (bpd) to the company’s current production capacity by late 2025. Venezuela’s total crude output has hovered around 850,000 bpd in recent months, according to data from the National Hydrocarbons Institute, with government targets set at 1 million bpd by year-end.

“PetroAndina’s investment is timely,” said Julio Rivas, energy analyst at Caracas-based consultancy Orinoco Insights. “With gradual improvements in field technology and stable local conditions, Venezuela is regaining its attractiveness for capital deployment in upstream projects. The focus on the Orinoco Belt reflects the region’s untapped potential.”

The expansion plans are expected to generate more than 1,200 direct jobs and an estimated 3,500 indirect positions throughout the supply chain. Local trade unions expressed optimism about the announcement, with Oil Workers Federation president Ricardo Méndez stating, “This project will provide valuable opportunities for skilled labor and help revitalize communities reliant on the oil sector.”

PetroAndina also indicated that a portion of the investment will be allocated to environmental initiatives, including the installation of gas capture systems and water treatment facilities. “Our approach is holistic,” added Contreras. “We’re aligning with international best practices to ensure responsible growth.”

The National Hydrocarbons Institute welcomed the initiative, with director Ana López emphasizing the importance of private and public collaboration. “Sustained investment is crucial to realize Venezuela’s energy ambitions,” López said.

Market observers will be watching closely as PetroAndina commences work on its upgraded facilities later this quarter, anticipating further momentum in the nation’s energy sector.
